items.streamTitle: Wearable thermal passthrough added bidirectional cues to augmented reality
items.streamSummary: A palm-mounted warm/cool AR prototype supported thermal passthrough and dynamic cues in human tests; moving patterns improved immersion while fingertip-contact realism declined. Benefits for practitioner learning remain untested.
items.attribution: Watkins, Ghosh, Chow and Sarkar — Communications Engineering (AR wearable prototype and human tests, November 13)

items.streamTitle: Four-wave misinformation dataset separated familiarity, accuracy, sharing and action
items.streamSummary: A new public dataset follows 1,153 of 1,422 initial Chinese participants across four February 2020 waves, separating claim familiarity, perceived accuracy, sharing and action measures. It is research infrastructure, not a causal misinformation result.
items.attribution: Chen, Zhang, Zhu and Xie — Scientific Data (public longitudinal data descriptor, November 13)

items.streamTitle: Multilingual language model separated psychological labels while retaining unestimable classes
items.streamSummary: NALU evaluated a multilingual, multitask psychological-language classifier on 589,155 unique Portuguese/English records; performance differed by construct, with insufficiently supported classes explicitly treated as unestimable.
items.attribution: Diego Resende Faria — Scientific Reports (multitask language-classification study, November 13)

items.streamTitle: Identity leadership predicted team identification and functioning across 11 countries
items.streamSummary: A 3,540-athlete study in 395 teams across 11 countries linked coaches' and peers' identity leadership with team identification, wellbeing and commitment; the cross-cultural consistency is observational, not a causal intervention effect.
items.attribution: Butalia et al. — Scientific Reports (cross-national observational team study, November 13)

items.streamTitle: Perspective-conflict reasoning predicted success in cooperative conversation after stroke
items.streamSummary: Among 31 right-hemisphere-stroke patients and 16 controls, partner-perspective reasoning predicted cooperative picture-description success beyond several cognitive controls. Small clinical observational data do not establish operational-team effects.
items.attribution: Suazo, Blake and Schnur — Scientific Reports (clinical social-cognition observational study, November 13)

items.streamTitle: Epi-LLM showed agent architecture and explicit attitudes shape modeled responses
items.streamSummary: Epi-LLM compared four LLM-agent architectures against epigame-related human evidence; simulated quarantine behavior varied with architecture and stated attitudes, while geographic labels alone did not ensure cultural fidelity.
items.attribution: Ferenz et al. — arXiv Epi-LLM preprint (behavioral agent-based simulation benchmark, June 1)

items.streamTitle: CAMO probed causal explanations inside generative social simulations
items.streamSummary: CAMO builds causal candidate graphs from LLM-agent traces and tests them with simulator counterfactual probes in four emergent settings. It identifies simulated mechanisms, not independently verified human causal pathways.
items.attribution: Yu, Guo, Hou, Xue and Ma — arXiv CAMO preprint (simulation causal-discovery methodology, April 16)

items.streamTitle: Chatbot warmth and usefulness correlated with distinct forms of perceived dependence
items.streamSummary: A November 12 survey of 345 Chinese chatbot users linked perceived empathy and usefulness to trust, attachment, functional reliance and self-reported difficulty controlling use; causal pathways and clinical addiction were not measured.
items.attribution: Yuan, Shi, Li and Zhao — Scientific Reports (cross-sectional survey; November 12)

items.streamTitle: Ukrainian student cohorts differed in self-trust and perceived control during war
items.streamSummary: Two independent Ukrainian student samples (2020 n=82; 2023 n=77) differed in self-trust and perceived control. Repeated cross-sectional comparison cannot isolate war-related causation.
items.attribution: Palamarchuk, Morska, Kolomiiets et al. — Scientific Reports (repeated cross-sectional study; November 12)

items.streamTitle: Dispersion of initial rumor spreaders increased simulated reach under specific stifling rules
items.streamSummary: November 12 simulations on synthetic and six real network structures found spaced initial rumor sources increased modeled reach under interaction-driven stifling. The result is conditional on diffusion rules, not validated human campaigning.
items.attribution: Ramrakhiyani, Tiwari and Vadivel Murugan — Scientific Reports (network rumor simulations; November 12)

items.streamTitle: ReA-Bench exposed failure modes hidden by overall AI-agent audit accuracy
items.streamSummary: A November 12 preprint introduced production-derived agent-audit challenges in six tiers, including paired context and missing-evidence cases; overall recall masks distinct failure mechanisms and legitimate-action false alarms.
items.attribution: Ye, Dai, Xie et al. — arXiv ReA-Bench preprint (agent auditing benchmark; November 12)

items.streamTitle: Russia and Belarus youth policies framed participation while limiting independent voice
items.streamSummary: A November 12 comparative document analysis found formal participation language in Russian and Belarusian youth policies coexisting with hierarchical, state-directed mobilization. Actual individual attitudes and effects were not directly measured.
items.attribution: Olga Vlasova — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications (comparative policy analysis; November 12)

items.streamTitle: Analysts followed randomized AI-agent preferences in consequential research choices
items.streamSummary: In a vendor-run randomized task, 50 analysts followed concealed, coin-flipped agent preferences on 86% of four methodological decisions; final-policy effects were more uncertain. An agent can shape judgment without necessarily being factually wrong.
items.attribution: Herdağdelen, Joren and Tamkin — Anthropic Research (randomized analyst study; October 27)

items.streamTitle: Digital Society Project released Version 8 indicators for political information environments
items.streamSummary: The Digital Society Project's 2026 Version 8 offers downloadable country-level time-series indicators on censorship, disinformation and foreign online influence. This is research infrastructure, not a new causal finding or direct audience measurement.
items.attribution: Digital Society Project — Version 8 (official cross-national dataset portal; 2026 update)

items.streamTitle: AI-enabled social marketing correlated with engagement and purchase intentions in China
items.streamSummary: A 620-consumer survey linked perceptions of generative-AI social marketing with brand engagement, relationship equity and purchase intentions. Structural-equation associations cannot establish actual purchase effects.
items.attribution: Jamil, Wang, Mustafa and Anwar — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications (cross-sectional consumer survey, November 11)

items.streamTitle: Monte Carlo power analysis offered clearer assumptions than AI-generated research participants
items.streamSummary: A November 11 Communications Psychology Comment argues that conventional Monte Carlo power planning exposes effect-size and variance assumptions while synthetic AI respondents bury unverified human-population assumptions in prompts.
items.attribution: Jamie Cummins — Communications Psychology (methodological Comment, November 11)

items.streamTitle: The Jastrow size illusion persisted across transformed stimuli, but not uniformly
items.streamSummary: Controlled judgments of matched stimuli found Jastrow-consistent size and numerosity biases across many geometric and object variants, but some outline faces did not differ from chance; stimulus context mattered.
items.attribution: Santacà and Granziol — Scientific Reports (human perceptual experiments, November 11)

items.streamTitle: France's AI council proposed vulnerability testing and information-crisis coordination
items.streamSummary: A government-appointed French commission used 55 consultations to develop 18 AI-vulnerability recommendations, including ex ante tests, anti-dependency design, crisis detection and election safeguards. They are proposals, not demonstrated protections.
items.attribution: Conseil de l'IA et du numérique (CIANum) — Protéger sans empêcher (official commission report, November 10)

items.streamTitle: Fast non-generative decision agents showed strong susceptibility to shopping nudges
items.streamSummary: Across three decision models and 600 runs per model, preselected defaults were chosen in 97.5–99.9% of trials, with social-proof information also changing choices. These are AI-agent choices, not human effects.
items.attribution: Kaltenpoth, Halimeh, Bösch and Müller — arXiv preprint (AI decision-model experiment, November 6)

items.streamTitle: Coupled adoption and opinion dynamics represented competing alternatives and switching
items.streamSummary: A two-layer MATE model linked exposure, social imitation, dissatisfaction and switching among multiple competing technologies, deriving coexistence equilibria and numerical control solutions. No human intervention forecasts were validated.
items.attribution: Alutto, Dabbene, Fontan, Johansson and Ravazzi — arXiv preprint (formal network-adoption model, November 3)

items.streamTitle: Opinion-network theory identified which social influence weights reduce collective bias
items.streamSummary: A Friedkin–Johnsen model reformulated susceptibility optimization as social-power allocation and derived conditions for optimal weights. The results are mathematical, not experimentally validated prescriptions for changing human conformity.
items.attribution: Tian, Sheng, Fontan, Wang and Johansson — arXiv preprint (formal social-influence optimization, November 2)

items.streamTitle: Correcting dependent AI reports mattered more than merely notifying their users
items.streamSummary: A 1,080-unit synthetic social-engineering study found publisher multiplicity did not increase already-high unsupported verification; corrections naming reused dependent reports improved repairs in tested workflows, with external authorization gates blocking illicit actions.
items.attribution: Bryan C. Boots — arXiv preprint, Networked Synthetic Social Engineering on the Web (controlled AI-service experiment, November 2)

items.streamTitle: IPTC mapped newsroom checkpoints where media-provenance metadata can fail
items.streamSummary: A media-industry technical framework maps C2PA Content Credentials from capture through newsroom editing and distribution, identifying metadata-loss points and verification checkpoints. It is an implementation design, not a measured decline in misinformation.
items.attribution: Fjellhaug, Armstrong and Quinn — IPTC/IBC technical paper announcement (September 28)

items.streamTitle: Near-eye infrared tracking enabled fast, lower-label VR gaze estimates
items.streamSummary: GazeShift released 2.1 million off-axis infrared images from 68 people and reported 1.84-degree calibrated VR gaze error with 5-ms headset inference. This is a sensing benchmark, not evidence of better training or attention.
items.attribution: Shapira, Goldin, Artyomov, Kim, Keller and Zehngut — arXiv preprint, GazeShift/VRGaze (VR sensing dataset, March 8)
